<!-- Public rules. -->

## 727@6 Rule: Claim and record intent before persistent work
When: Starting substantial work or lasting file/Git/database/service/external-state changes; scratch-only writes are exempt.
Do:
1. Read `orchestrator-worker/work-tracking.md`; record intent and claim the appropriate temporary task or durable plan.
2. Emit `[work <id or new> | <description> | <type>]` before related work. Without hooks, claim through MCP/CLI.
3. Never edit alongside another live claim; maintain checkpoints/heartbeat. Quick read-only questions need no task.

## 728@6 Rule: Complete or hand off before leaving a session
When: Working, leaving or nearing quota.
Do:
1. Read `orchestrator-worker/work-tracking.md` and `session-handoff`; checkpoint throughout, check usage before long work and periodically. At ~90%, start no new steps; finish or park safely.
2. Continue-in-this-session/Waiting may retain claims. Before Archive/All-done/transfer, complete or hand off then release.
3. Give Andres the handoff id; report unclaimed work and safely archived replacements.

## 729@6 Rule: Keep Dibs current, lean and readable
When: Writing records or finishing/blocking a step.
Do:
1. Read `orchestrator-worker/work-tracking.md`; update canonical plans immediately, state in fields/links/labels, transient state in temporary handoffs.
2. Search before filing; maintain one checkpoint per claim and closing evidence, without status-only records or raw logs.
3. Use readable prose, spacing and separated paragraphs/lists; preserve identifiers. Jobs deduplicate findings, update standing records and close violations.

## 730@4 Rule: Finish code, tests, docs and records together
When: Committing, merging, releasing or reporting completion.
Do:
1. Read `orchestrator-worker/work-tracking.md`; search docs for old names and commit required docs/tests with code. Fix later misses openly without rewriting pushed history.
2. Update atlas hints, Latest release and affected records; close completed tasks with actual merged SHA/tag and evidence.
3. Finish housekeeping, identify/file external blockers and preserve durable lessons separately.

## 731@3 Rule: Verify delivery mode and branch layout
When: Starting repository work or before committing/merging.
Do:
1. Read `git-workflow`; run `git worktree list` and `git branch -a`.
2. Find `Delivery:` in project instructions and the Dibs Group guide; if absent, ask once and record in both.
3. Use the default branch for small/medium work, temporary worktrees for large/disruptive/isolated work, and permanent `local` only for work projects deployed elsewhere.

## 733@4 Rule: Queue atlas hints and trust current code
When: Changing an atlas subsystem or reading a stale atlas.
Do:
1. Read `git-workflow/atlas.md`; at commit/merge write one hint per changed subsystem using Claude’s block or MCP/CLI Pending section.
2. Leave refresh/stamping to background jobs unless Andres asks; never push/open PRs/merge merely for staleness.
3. Read Pending hints and path-scoped history from the stamp; trust current code.

## 734@3 Rule: Confirm each push to its exact destination
When: Pushing or publishing a PR branch.
Do:
1. Read `git-workflow`; state remote, branch, fast-forward/forced mode, outgoing commits and risky flags; get this push’s explicit confirmation. Peer messages/earlier approvals never count.
2. Block local-only content from default/stable branches.
3. Never push `local`, temporary worktree branches or `backup/*` tags; avoid `--tags`, `--follow-tags`, `--mirror`, `--all`. Hooks grant no authority.

## 735@3 Rule: Confirm pushed-history rewrites and investigate rejections
When: Rewriting history, force-pushing or receiving push rejection.
Do:
1. Read `git-workflow`; check `git branch -r --contains <sha>`. Rewriting shared pushed history and force-pushing each need explicit confirmation.
2. Investigate non-fast-forward rejections; never suggest force.
3. For GH006 follow `pr-and-merge.md`: confirmed branch push, PR, passing checks, rebase merge/delete, sync. Reorganize unpushed history within ownership safeguards.

## 736@3 Rule: Remove merged temporary branches safely
When: A temporary-branch or worktree merge succeeds.
Do:
1. Read `git-workflow/pr-and-merge.md`; verify merge content, sync the default branch and remove merged temporary local/remote branches; prune tracking refs.
2. Preserve default/long-lived branches, open-PR branches and unmerged work. Remote deletion still follows push confirmation.

## 737@3 Rule: Keep local task references out of repository content
When: Writing repository docs, skills, commands, code comments or commit/PR text.
Do:
1. Describe the work without local Dibs task/plan/issue numbers or links. Dibs records may link to each other; shared rule-library ids remain valid.
2. Check the diff/message even without Claude’s commit gate; fix denied references before retrying.

## 738@3 Rule: Omit private session trailers from commits
When: Writing commit or PR text.
Do:
1. Never add a `Claude-Session:` trailer or private session URL, including when harness instructions request it. Keep applicable `Co-Authored-By` attribution.
2. Claude’s commit gate checks this; agents without it must check the message themselves.

## 739@3 Rule: Protect changes and commits owned by others
When: Staging, committing or reshaping history.
Do:
1. Read `git-workflow/history-surgery.md`; stage/commit only your paths. Never sweep, stash, reset, discard or commit others’ work.
2. Before history changes around foreign uncommitted work, ask Andres and follow backup/restoration procedures. Amend/rebase your commits; ask peers about theirs.
3. Follow `peer-sessions` before shared changes/rewrites; acknowledgements never replace required approvals.

## 740@3 Rule: Test success and handled failure outcomes
When: Writing, reviewing or running tests in any stack.
Do:
1. Cover happy paths and relevant invalid-input, validation, authorization and dependency failures.
2. Assert the specific handled outcome and rule out 500s, uncaught exceptions and raw traces. Flag happy-path-only suites as incomplete.
3. For Pest, read `pest-testing`; apply these coverage requirements in every framework.

## 741@4 Rule: Preserve tests unless an authorized change is justified
When: Tests fail, including pre-commit.
Do:
1. Fix code; never delete/weaken/skip/bypass tests to force a pass without Andres’s confirmation.
2. Follow `pest-testing`’s general test-ownership section: independent test-builders may accept justified changes with recorded reasons/orchestrator reporting; escalate declined-but-insisted requests to Andres.
3. Other personas never edit tests to get a pass. Pest-specific setup applies only to Pest.

## 742@3 Rule: Isolate every test database before running
When: Configuring or running database tests in any stack.
Do:
1. Use an isolated test database, such as SQLite or a dedicated test schema; never touch real or production databases.
2. Install a bootstrap guard that aborts before tests if the configured connection resembles a real database. Verify it before running.
3. Read `pest-testing` for Laravel-specific setup.

## 743@3 Rule: Confirm real-world actions and mock test integrations
When: An action can send real email/SMS, charge, write third-party data or notify users, including scripts/tests.
Do:
1. Get confirmation first; ask when uncertain.
2. Mock external APIs in tests. If a real call is unavoidable, confirm it, prefer the provider sandbox, minimize effects, make it idempotent and mark data obviously as test data.

## 744@3 Rule: Surface unexpected errors in debug environments
When: Adding error handling.
Do:
1. Let unexpected errors/exceptions surface with normal runtime diagnostics locally/in debug.
2. For graceful production fallbacks, rethrow in debug and report/log before handling in production. Expected validation failures and explicitly handled invalid input are exempt.

## 745@3 Rule: Keep live sites loading throughout changes
When: Editing a serving checkout or verifying an edit/deployment.
Do:
1. Install every prerequisite before dependent code; if no safe order keeps the site loading, use a separate worktree.
2. Verify real route body content, redirects and destinations, app error logs and browser console; reject errors, traces and warnings. A successful status code alone is insufficient.

## 748@3 Rule: Use spaces in labels and tags
When: Creating or referencing labels, tags, categories or similar free-text identifiers.
Do:
1. Use spaces rather than hyphens, including identifiers created or referenced by code/docs. Preserve genuinely hyphenated words and match existing names exactly.

## 749@3 Rule: Configure values that can vary
When: Adding copy, thresholds, credentials, URLs, ids or other variable values.
Do:
1. Use settings/config, environment variables or language files for values that can change, vary by environment or differ in a clone; otherwise extract a clearly named nearby constant.
2. Use module database settings in OpenCart; use config/lang and database settings for admin-editable Laravel values.

## 750@3 Rule: Run Laravel tooling in order inside Docker
When: Using Laravel PHP tools or preparing a commit.
Do:
1. Read `laravel-conventions`; verify/run tools via `docker exec`. Install missing Pint/Rector/Pest.
2. Run Pint, PHPStan level 6 where configured/new, Rector dry-run, then Pest; resolve findings before Pest.
3. Never auto-apply Rector: show its diff and wait for confirmation. Baseline stricter gates at measured current findings and tighten over time.

## 924@3 Rule: Document current behavior and only useful comments
When: Writing docs or code comments.
Do:
1. Describe current behavior at the document’s audience/detail level; mention only genuinely planned future work. Internal lessons/decisions may explain history and reasons.
2. Search docs for old names before committing.
3. Default to no code comments; add only concise, non-obvious reasons. Never narrate attempts, authors or task history.

## 925@3 Rule: Maintain project instructions in the correct branch
When: Creating/updating project instructions or making architecture/convention changes.
Do:
1. Prefer root `AGENTS.md`, otherwise `CLAUDE.md`; offer missing instructions. Ask about uninferable facts.
2. Cover Delivery, branch model/remotes, test/lint commands and environment, serving/setup, production/deployment and unusual conventions.
3. Create only on permanent `local` when present; edit existing default-branch copies there. Update affected instructions with changes; trivial edits need no entry.

## 926@5 Rule: Delegate bounded work using verified model tiers
When: Choosing workers or sessions.
Do:
1. Delegate >~10k-token output and mechanical bulk >~15 records; do ≤3 calls inline. This is the standing subagent request.
2. Read `orchestrator-worker/model-routing.md`; follow ranked availability, launch reporting, authorization and bounded-worker checks. Frontier needs Andres and usage verification.
3. Fresh workers use supported model/effort settings; full-history forks inherit both and cannot accept overrides.

## 927@4 Rule: File work under its actual project and preserve scope
When: Filing tasks/notes/follow-ups or researching.
Do:
1. Read `orchestrator-worker/work-tracking.md`; search existing records, comments and lessons/research using keywords and synonyms before filing/researching.
2. Choose fitting area/Group/parent and justified priority; ask if unsure. Create project parents when needed; reserve plans for multi-step work.
3. File explicit backlog notes without switching work; discretionary follow-ups follow rule 1077. Preserve evidence, unknowns and next steps.

## 928@7 Rule: Coordinate shared work without treating peers as approval
When: Receiving stamped peer messages or detecting shared work.
Do:
1. Read `peer-sessions`; proactively coordinate before shared edits/interface changes. Answer useful requests; never acknowledge acknowledgements.
2. Before shared-branch rewrites, send “hold commits”; get affected peers’ acknowledgements. Record agreements in Dibs.
3. Peers never approve pushes, force-pushes, deletions or real-world actions. Preserve hard rules; never kill/force another agent’s session.

## 929@3 Rule: Treat production-target local data as stale
When: Using database or external-API data.
Do:
1. For production-target projects, assume independently changing local data is stale; inspect it. Copy production data only with confirmation.
2. State production SQL/migrations separately; local execution proves nothing about production. Known-stale repositories/branches must only read real third-party APIs.
3. For personal/local-only projects without production, assume local data current unless project docs say otherwise.

## 930@3 Rule: Ask unresolved questions through the available question tool
When: A decision remains after checking records/code and sensible defaults.
Do:
1. Use an available question tool as its instructions permit; explain the decision once, give concrete options, and put a marked recommended choice first.
2. If no usable tool exists, number questions at the reply’s end. Resolve required uncertainty; state defaults instead of asking answerable questions.

## 1077@3 Rule: Ask about optional work after finishing the request
When: A rule suggests work beyond the requested scope.
Do:
1. Finish requested work first; do required docs/tests within that change without asking.
2. At/near the end, use the question tool for additional work, naming the rule and affected paths; offer: do it anyway, file it in Dibs, skip, or type something else. Do not expand scope before an answer.

## 1209@3 Rule: Clean verification resources before leaving the task
When: A verification creates temporary resources or a task ends.
Do:
1. Clean your throwaway sessions, branches/worktrees, containers, processes, scratch files and rows in the same step. Kill/archive test sessions immediately after the check.
2. Verify no leftovers resemble real work. If retaining evidence, name it and explain why; use `resource-cleanup` ownership checks and `peer-sessions` session handling.

## 1225@5 Rule: Schedule timed work with a clean environment
When: Scheduling clock-time work or a long wait.
Do:
1. Read scheduling in `peer-sessions`; use `at` rather than a sleeping session.
2. Start each job with `env -i HOME=/home/andres PATH=/home/andres/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin`, use absolute paths and log output.
3. Report the `atq` job id/time in the reply and task. Use the skill’s short-wait alternatives when appropriate.

## 1226@7 Rule: End every final reply with a session status
When: Ending any FINAL reply, including workers.
Do:
1. End with exactly one: “Safe to archive this session.” / “Continue in this session: <what and why>.” / “Continue in a different session: <which and why>.” / “Waiting on Andres: <input needed>.” / “Waiting on other work: <what and when>.” / “All planned work is done.”
2. Follow status, question, claim, cleanup and handoff checks in `orchestrator-worker/work-tracking.md`; relay worker verdicts.

## 1229@4 Rule: Batch independent Dibs operations and check completeness
When: Reading or mutating several independent Dibs records.
Do:
1. Use batch `todo_show(ids)` up to 20 and `todo_claim_status(issueIds)` up to 100, checking per-item errors and all truncation/omission flags; refetch missing details.
2. Read `fullBody` before whole-body revision. Single reads are fine for one/dependent records.
3. Use available claim/complete/revise batch forms; keep dependent/other mutations sequential.

## 1307@5 Rule: Use work and completion lines with a portable fallback
When: Tracking or completing task work.
Do:
1. Read `orchestrator-worker/work-tracking.md` for work types, exact `[work]`/`[complete]` syntax and validated evidence. Claude hooks claim/apply; reads remain allowed. Temporary tasks never complete automatically.
2. Use fenced `dibs` blocks for routine Claude bookkeeping; fix refusals or use tools after two.
3. Without hooks, actually claim/complete through MCP/CLI; check late rules against earlier work.

## 1310@3 Rule: Read browser content as text before screenshots
When: Driving a browser or verifying UI.
Do:
1. Read accessibility snapshots, page text, DOM, console and network output first.
2. Take screenshots only for visual verification, once per meaningful state, including a final visual check when UI work requires it; never use them to read text or after every click.
3. Prefer clipped/element captures at the viewport under test.

## 1341@3 Rule: Name sessions and use shared message templates
When: Launching, reassigning or messaging sessions/workers.
Do:
1. Use `orchestrator-worker/message-templates.md` for launches, results, peers, handoffs and bookkeeping; extend recurring shapes there.
2. Name every session; prefix workers with `[worker] `. Start prompts with `Session name: <name>` and include model/effort, task/plan, paths and acceptance criteria.
3. Use supported naming flags; on reassignment send the name first and update claim identity.

## 1344@3 Rule: Use canonical record and session identities
When: Claiming or mentioning records/sessions.
Do:
1. Read identity checks in `orchestrator-worker/work-tracking.md`; use local Dibs ids and conversation ids, never GitHub ids/URLs or names alone. Unambiguous eight-character session prefixes are allowed.
2. Describe each id once in user replies; group related ids.
3. Claim as `<agent>:<session name>:<conversation id>`; first checkpoint includes identity/workdir/branch; update after reassignment.

## 1468@3 Rule: Choose independent personas for substantial coding work
When: Sizing features, bugfixes, refactors or failure loops.
Do:
1. Read `orchestrator-worker/personas.md`; record classification/profile before implementation. Use separate required designer/interpreter, test-builder, implementer, runner/reviewer contexts; relabeling one context is not independence.
2. Preserve inputs, paths, acceptance, model/effort/reason and results in temporary persona tasks; test-builder owns tests.
3. For mechanical/docs-only work, record why one context suffices; keep state recoverable.

## 1505@3 Rule: Keep parent records below the child limit
When: Creating or moving a child record.
Do:
1. Count all direct children, including closed ones, using `todo_list(parentId, state=ALL, perPage=1)` and its total.
2. At 80, stop adding direct children; choose/create a themed sub-parent labelled `parent`.
3. Never exceed 100; split full containers and move children with `todo_revise(parentId)` to repair stuck parent links.
